description: Fix the explored Node configuration-admission comparison in three histories: hold_advance, early_advance, apply_then_advance. For each actual first configuration committed at first_index, record caller application state immediately before second proposal, observe the second appended entry type, and then finish all application duties. Compare only the required implication: if first was unapplied at proposal, the second must not remain EntryConfChange. Apply-first is a permitted-path diagnostic without a mandatory acceptance oracle.

harness.description: Actual Node goroutine and public API, one initial voter and sequential learner additions, synchronous MemoryStorage persistence. Context timeout and bounded Ready loops fail prerequisites rather than report protocol violations.
semantic_changes: No target changes; MemoryStorage substitutes completed durability and absent learners receive no network messages.
Separate userApplied counter advances only after caller application/ApplyConfChange; Status.Applied is recorded independently.

legality.derivation: Public RestartNode starts a single voter from snapshot index/term 1 and matching HardState/Applied. Campaign and Ready/Advance create actual leader commitment. Persist all entries and HardState, preserve application order, and defer only first ApplyConfChange under Node early-Advance permission. Propose the second via public Node, use Status as a serialization fence, inspect emitted entries, then finish application in original order. The hold and apply-first controls vary only the Advance/application placement. Messages to unavailable learners may be dropped; no peer vote or acknowledgment is forged.
legality.applicability: Node API, synchronous Ready/Advance, prior committed config not rejected by caller and deferred ApplyConfChange, ordered eventual application.
unresolved: An unstated configuration-specific exception to early Advance would change applicability; it is not present in the captured Node/package contract.
alternatives: Interpreting all Advance calls as completed application contradicts the Node-specific early-Advance permission, although that stronger description occurs on RawNode.

grounding.derivation: Admission event records actual prior caller application before the second public proposal; result retains that captured value and the actual appended Entry.Type. Identity scenario+first_index correlates each independent history. The implication only forbids a configuration entry when prior_applied_at_proposal is false. Held-Advance result may be emitted after caller later applies the first change, so current user_applied is not substituted for admission-time state. No result filtering by expected type occurs.

observable_properties.description: When the preceding committed configuration was still unapplied at second-proposal admission, the second proposal must be dropped/replaced rather than retained as an EntryConfChange.

uncertainties: The applicability interpretation uses explicit Node early-Advance permission; RawNode completion wording is stronger and not used to authorize the history.
Only local admission of learner changes is measured; safety or availability consequences require a different legal history.
